# Pro maioribus {-#literature}

Everything that I've learnt has come from one of the many remarkable monographs and texts that others have written. What follows is a selection of those that I recommend without hesitation to anyone wishing to understand these ideas more deeply.

**The statistical analysis of time series.** Anderson, TW (1971). 

_Whilst notionally a book about time series, it is really about much more. I picked it up to understand the covariance structure of the periodogram and found, instead, a first glimpse into the rich mathematical world that underpins so much of what we take for granted in statistical modelling._

**Asymptotic statistics.** Van der Vaart, AW (2000). 

_This book is the reason these notes exist: it is proof that brilliance and accessibility rarely coincide. This is the book that made me want to know more, but didn't slow down to help. These notes are the record of me, painfully, figuring it out._

**Linear algebra done right.** Axler, S (2024). 

_I wish this was how I was taught linear algebra. Axler replaces the rote manipulation of matrices with an emphasis on structure, abstraction, and proof. The book is an antidote to every course that began with Gaussian elimination and never recovered._
